name: Telecom CDR fraud (wholesale / IRSF / bypass)
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Three layers of competition sit underneath telecom CDR fraud detection today and beava is closest to the bottom layer. (a) Generic streaming + feature-serving substrate that in-house carrier and CPaaS fraud teams build on: Apache Flink (the dominant CDR streaming choice today - Nussknacker's 'Real-time Telco Fraud Detection' case study built on Flink is the canonical public reference, plus Confluent / Ververica CDR-streaming material), Apache Kafka / Kafka Streams / ksqlDB, Apache Spark Real-Time Mode, Redis (still common as a hot-counter store, now competing with Apache-2.0 Valkey shipped as the redis package in Ubuntu 26.04), Aerospike (explicit telecom AI/ML case-study material covering billing/charging + fraud + policy + subscriber data; Apache-2.0 community + proprietary Enterprise), SingleStore (publishes a CDR-fraud vector-functions example), Materialize / RisingWave (SQL streaming substitutes for Flink), and the ML feature stores Tecton (Databricks Aug 2025, $900M), Fennel (Databricks Apr 2025), Feast, Hopsworks, Chalk - none of which today ship a telecom-vertical product. The dominant production pattern in carrier fraud teams is still 'CDR mediation -> Kafka -> Flink -> Redis-or-Aerospike -> Drools/vendor rules engine + ML scorer -> SBC/SMSC enforcement'. (b) Open-source telecom-fraud-adjacent stacks at the application layer: CGRates (real-time charging system with fraud-detection + auto-mitigation hooks, MPL-2.0), BillRun (open-source billing + anti-fraud system, AGPL-3.0), tinega04/telecom-fraud-detection (academic CDR-ML notebook, no production positioning), TeleAntiFraud (MM-25 audio-text fraud dataset, not a runtime), zsoltmester/anomaly-detector (CDR anomaly notebook). None are real-time feature-substrate competitors; CGRates is the closest in shape. (c) The closed-loop telecom fraud-management platforms themselves (see competitive_incumbent_per_domain). Beava does NOT compete with layer (c) - those are buyers, embedding partners, or untouchable incumbents with 20-year tier-1 carrier relationships. Beava competes at layer (a) by collapsing the (Kafka+Flink+Redis-or-Aerospike) substrate into a single binary, with a secondary overlap with layer (b) only at the open-source-telecom-stack rule-author level although beava ships no rules engine of its own.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: The telecom-fraud-management platform incumbents that buyers procure as black boxes - beava is NOT competing with these directly at the product layer, it is the infrastructure they could be built on (or that they have built proprietary equivalents of). Funding/scale/M&A as of 2025-2026: Subex (Indian-listed, INR 293 Cr revenue FY March 2025, ROC Fraud Management 8.3+ with 'Online Statistical Rules' for real-time IRSF, multi-year tier-1 deals incl. MTN Group 5-year deal across 14 networks, tier-1 Middle East operator multi-year renewal, tier-1 European operator extension, completed Security Analytics Fabric AI acquisition Jan 2026 to bolster threat detection); Mobileum (filed Chapter 11 SDTX 23 Jul 2024 with prepack plan, exited 12 Sep 2024 after eliminating ~$530M of debt via $60M new-money DIP + $100M roll-up, H.I.G. Capital lost equity to lender group, 1,000+ customers in 150+ countries pre-restructuring, separately in Feb 2026 the former CFO and Chief of Delivery were criminally charged with securities fraud over the 2022 $915M Audax->H.I.G. sale - the brand is operational but the trust and reference-customer story is materially impaired); Neural Technologies ActivML (claims '99% of SIM box activity within 10 minutes', long-standing tier-1 carrier references); Hiya (B2B + CSP branded calling, $30.7M total funding across 3 rounds, now live on Vodafone UK extending verified caller ID to ~100% of UK mobile subscribers, also on EE and O2/Three, focused on caller ID + scam-call protection not IRSF/AIT); LATRO Networks (Fraud Shield + AI-powered SIM/bypass detection, repeatedly ranked top simbox-detection supplier by independent surveys); SIGOS (German, leads test-call services + equipment, top-tier simbox detection per Commsrisk surveys); BICS (FraudGuard - crowdsourced fraud prevention across global roaming partner network, monitors international signaling for IRSF and triggers automated blocks across vast partner network, owned by Proximus, deeply embedded in interconnect-settlement flow); Enea (acquired AdaptiveMobile Security 2021 for EUR 45M, runs Adaptive Messaging Firewall + Adaptive Signaling Firewall + Messaging Intelligence covering SS7/Diameter/GTP-C/5G and AIT, TextNow partnership 2025); Symsoft (Sinch division, A2P SMS firewall + fraud); NetCracker (powers BICS, OSS + fraud modules); Amdocs / Nokia / Ericsson / Tech Mahindra / TCS / SAS Fraud Management / FICO / IBM (i2 + Safer Payments) / HPE - tier-1 carrier infrastructure incumbents; XConnect (Somos-owned, partnered with GSMA Jan 2025 to embed GSMA IRSF Prevention data into IRSFCheck, >90% detection rate, IPRN database refreshed every 20 seconds); AB Handshake (mutual-call-validation protocol, 99.99% claimed accuracy, partnerships with iconectiv + Orca Wave); TransNexus (STIR/SHAKEN + robocall mitigation, US-focused); TNS (robocall mitigation + branded calling); iconectiv (US numbering authority); Sinch + Twilio + Bandwidth + Vonage + Infobip + Plivo (CPaaS players have built or are building their own AIT/Fraud Guards in-house - see CPaaS section); Sardine (SMS pumping protection layered on fraud + risk platform, $145M total funding, FRAML positioning); GSMA itself runs IRSF Prevention as an industry service (operator-paid subscription, 90%+ detection on confirmed cases, 20-second database refresh) plus the GLF/i3Forum Code of Conduct signed by 22+ international carriers and the CFCA fraud-loss survey ($41.82B global telecom fraud loss in 2025 vs $38.95B in 2023, IRSF $6.23B, 48% of operators reporting high-volume IRSF attacks). Mobileum's bankruptcy plus the criminal-fraud charges against former executives is a genuine 2024-2026 incumbent-disruption event that no other vertical in the map has - a credible second-place RAFM vendor is operationally damaged and the buyer narrative 'pick the safe choice' is weaker than it was.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Proprietary-dominant with very few open-source options at the telecom-vertical layer. The tier-1 fraud-management incumbents (Subex, Mobileum, Neural Technologies, LATRO, SIGOS, BICS, Enea AdaptiveMobile, Hiya, NetCracker, Amdocs, Nokia, Ericsson, SAS, FICO, IBM, XConnect, AB Handshake, TransNexus, Symsoft) are all closed-source proprietary licensed appliances or SaaS; pricing and contract terms are negotiated per tier-1 carrier and not public. The feature-substrate layer beava competes at is mixed: Apache Flink (Apache-2.0), Kafka (Apache-2.0), Valkey (BSD-3-Clause, replacing Redis in Ubuntu 26.04 and most cloud defaults), Aerospike (proprietary Enterprise + Apache-2.0 community), Redis (post-AGPLv3/SSPL relicense), SingleStore (proprietary), Materialize/RisingWave (BSL), Tecton (Databricks proprietary), Feast (Apache-2.0). Open-source telecom-adjacent at the application layer: CGRates (MPL-2.0, real-time charging + fraud hooks), BillRun (AGPL-3.0, billing + anti-fraud - AGPL is a known dealbreaker for closed-source product embedders), Fonoster (Apache-2.0 'open-source Twilio alternative', no fraud-specific subsystem). Beava's Apache-2.0 with no open-core split is therefore a genuine and unusual posture in this segment - one of the very few Apache-2.0 options at the feature-substrate layer that also speaks the telecom-fraud primitive vocabulary (per-A-number / per-B-prefix velocities, distinct-B-country fan-out, duration distributions), and a clean alternative for CPaaS providers and MVNOs who want to ship in-house AIT/IRSF controls without an open-core rug-pull or AGPL contamination. License is rarely a procurement filter for tier-1 carriers (they will pay for proprietary if Subex/Mobileum/LATRO solve the audit story) but it IS a filter for CPaaS engineering teams choosing what to embed.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: Low. Telecom CDR fraud is one of the few segments in the map where the hyperscaler bundling threat is genuinely low, for three structural reasons: (1) Carrier-grade compliance and air-gap posture - tier-1 carrier fraud platforms live inside the operator's data centre or a regulated colo for ePrivacy / national CDR-retention / GDPR / lawful-intercept-adjacent reasons; AWS/GCP/Azure-native bundles are a hard procurement sell to a tier-1 carrier security team and almost universally rejected for the SBC/SMSC enforcement path itself, though they show up for analytical-tier batch CDR processing. (2) SBC/SMSC integration is the procurement gate, not the feature store - the integration work that defines a winning vendor is the SBC/SMSC/CGF tap (Oracle ACME, Ribbon, AudioCodes, Sansay, Mavenir, Metaswitch + Mavenir/Ericsson/Nokia/OpenMind/NewNet SMSCs + 3GPP TS 32.298 ASN.1 CGF), and no hyperscaler ships a telecom-vertical SBC/SMSC adapter library - they ship generic streaming. (3) GSMA IRSF Prevention as the de-facto industry data layer - the hot-list / IPRN data fed into XConnect, Subex, Mobileum, Hiya, Enea is GSMA-licensed, not hyperscaler-bundled, and that licensing is the actual moat. That said, two real bundling vectors exist for adjacent buyers: (a) CPaaS providers (Twilio, Sinch, Vonage, Bandwidth, Plivo, Infobip) are running their own AIT detection in-house on AWS/GCP/Azure today using Kinesis/Kafka + DynamoDB/Bigtable/CosmosDB - the hyperscaler IS the feature substrate for the CPaaS sub-segment; (b) Databricks + Tecton (Aug 2025) + Fennel (Apr 2025) + Snowflake Dynamic Tables increasingly host CDR analytical-tier feature pipelines for carrier-side data-platform teams. Neither of these bundles a sub-ms TCP feature store at the SBC/SMSC pre-routing hop, which is exactly the latency regime beava plays in, so the bundling threat at the real-time blocking decision is materially lower than for any other segment in the map.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Heterogeneous and notably NOT Kafka-only - the best-fit segment for beava's HTTP/TCP-push model relative to the rest of the map. Upstream producers in carrier-side deployments: SBC CDR taps (Oracle ACME / Ribbon / AudioCodes / Sansay / Mavenir / Metaswitch typically via RADIUS-Accounting, syslog, or proprietary push), SMSC EDR taps (Mavenir / Ericsson / Nokia / OpenMind / NewNet), billing-mediation outputs (Amdocs / NetCracker / Comarch / MATRIXX / Volt Active Data emit CDRs at intervals or as streams), DPI / signaling probes (Polystar, ELLA Communications, Cisco Joy), 3GPP charging gateways (CGF emitting GTP'-encapsulated CDRs per TS 32.298 ASN.1 BER), and CPaaS internal event buses (Twilio / Sinch / Vonage proprietary - typically HTTP/JSON or in-house gRPC). The streaming-pipeline shops (Subex ROC, Mobileum, Neural Technologies, Nussknacker-Flink rigs) typically run Kafka in the middle, and some carrier billing-mediation systems publish to Kafka topics natively. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 and framed-TCP :8081 (msgpack) map cleanly to (a) the SBC syslog / RADIUS-tap path with a thin adapter, (b) the CPaaS internal HTTP/REST event bus directly, and (c) MVNO / IoT-MVNO billing-mediation REST outputs directly - many smaller MVNOs and CPaaS shops do not run Kafka at all and have no appetite for it. A thin Kafka consumer is needed for the streaming-pipeline shops and is not in v0 (~few hundred lines of Rust). Downstream consumers are (i) the rules engine - often Drools, FEEL, or vendor-proprietary inside Subex/Mobileum/LATRO/Symsoft, (ii) the ML scorer - XGBoost / LightGBM / GNN (recent academic work uses graph-based latent-synergy models, plus deep learning for SIM-box bypass detection), and (iii) the SOAR / SBC enforcement plane via SIP redirect / SMSC drop / API-key throttle. The downstream coupling is HTTP/JSON-friendly (batch_get well-fit for 20-80 features per decision per the NDSS-2021 paper and Sinapsio's 150-call-parameter feature catalogue) and is one of the strongest 'natural fit' signals for beava in the entire map.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Hard velocity caps and GLF/i3Forum Code-of-Conduct-aligned rules ('no more than N minutes to b_country in T from a fresh subscription', 'block all calls to GSMA IRSF-Prevention-flagged b_prefix with refresh <20s') belong in a rules engine (Drools / FEEL / Subex's vendor DSL / Mobileum's vendor DSL). ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM / increasingly graph-neural-networks per the latent-synergy-graph approach published 2023, plus deep learning for SIM-box bypass) consume beava features for the longer-tail signatures. Beava sits below both as the feature substrate and ships no rules engine of its own. Note: the carrier fraud rules engine is NOT regulator-validated in the SR-11-7 / EBA sense (telecom fraud is liability-grade, not regulator-grade like AML), so beava being feature-serving-only is a feature here, not a bug - it keeps the model-validation perimeter on the rules and ML team, where it belongs.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Six concrete reasons a buyer in this segment would pick beava over the incumbent / hyperscaler bundle, calibrated to the wedge described in the prompt (cannot displace Subex/Mobileum at tier-1 carriers; COULD be the velocity-feature backend for new MVNOs / IoT-MVNOs / fintech-telco hybrids and CPaaS engineering teams): (1) Single binary collapses the (Kafka + Flink + Redis-or-Aerospike + feature-store ETL) stack into one process for fraud-operations teams that are explicitly NOT data-platform teams - a 20-person MVNO or a 5-person CPaaS fraud-ops squad cannot operate Flink + Kafka + Redis in production and the addressable buyer here is precisely that team. (2) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives (counters, velocities, distinct-counts via HLL, distributions via t-digest, ratios) cover exactly the features Subex / Mobileum / Neural Technologies hand-code: per-A-number 1m/5m/1h/24h call+minute counts, distinct-B-country fan-out, duration distributions (flat-distribution signature for SIM-box), outbound/inbound ratio, per-(A,B-country) never-before-called flag, per-app/per-MCCMNC pair AIT counters with sequential-MSISDN ratio. (3) Sub-millisecond TCP get / batch_get fits inside the SBC / SMSC / SMS-firewall pre-routing budget (10-50 ms for SIP INVITE / MO-SMS forwarding, 100-500 ms for CPaaS OTP-send pre-submission) with comfortable margin, enabling true in-flight blocking rather than the hour-batch retrospective detection that most legacy CDR-mediation pipelines still run. The NDSS-2021 IRSF paper validates 98% accuracy / 0.28% FPR using this exact feature class. (4) Push-on-event ingestion (HTTP/JSON :8080, framed-TCP :8081 msgpack) accepts CDR feeds directly from SBC / SMSC / billing-mediation tap or CPaaS internal HTTP bus without requiring Kafka in the path - decisive for MVNOs, IoT-MVNOs, fintech-telco hybrids, and smaller CPaaS shops that do not run Kafka and have no appetite for the SRE cost. (5) Apache-2.0 with no open-core split and no acquisition risk is a genuine wedge in 2025-2026 against (a) the Mobileum bankruptcy + criminal-fraud-charge narrative that has materially damaged the 'safe choice' positioning of the #2 RAFM vendor, (b) the Redis-post-relicense + Valkey split now resolved cloud-default in Valkey's favor, (c) the AGPL contamination of BillRun, and (d) procurement risk for CPaaS providers competing on AIT controls who do not want an open-core rug under their differentiator. (6) ~684k EPS sustained on a single Apple-M4 core (TCP + msgpack + parallel=16, per beava's published benchmark) means a single 1U at the PoP-edge alongside the SBC can cover the entire site's CDR fan-out for a small/mid MVNO (10-50 EPS to 1k-10k EPS) and most CPaaS sub-tenants - tier-1 throughput (50k-200k sustained, >1M busy-hour bursts at >100M-subscriber operators) sits inside the single-node ceiling with margin but multi-region active-active aggregation requires features beava does not yet have.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete gaps blocking production telecom-fraud deployments today (derived from use case 25 open_engineering_gaps and SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md v0 invariants). These are SEVERE in number but less audit-grade than AML (V7) - telecom-fraud is liability-grade, not regulator-validated-model-grade: (1) No TLS on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 and no mTLS - tier-1 telcos run strict network-segmentation audits, this is an instant non-starter without a sidecar TLS terminator and even with one the auditor will ask 'is the listener authenticated?'. (2) No AuthN/AuthZ - API-key auth scoped per namespace is the minimum bar; JWT/OIDC + per-topic / per-entity-grain ACLs are needed for multi-tenant CPaaS hosting. (3) No triggers / no 'fire when counter crosses threshold' - the SINGLE highest-impact missing primitive for this domain per use case 25's trigger_action_required (rated 'strongly required'); the difference between 'detect IRSF in 60 s' and 'detect IRSF after 0.5 billed minutes' is direct interconnect-settlement P&L; fraud teams want 'when a_number_hash crosses threshold T in window W, emit BLOCK action to a webhook / SBC SIP-redirect / Kafka topic' as a primitive, today the buyer must poll. (4) No multi-tenancy / no namespace ACLs - a CPaaS vendor cannot safely host multiple enterprise customers' AIT controls on one beava box; a wholesale carrier cannot safely host multiple downstream-operator views; a managed-fraud-service vendor cannot safely host multiple carrier customers. (5) No in-process sharding - global tier-1 (>100 M subs, 300M+ subscriber state, hundreds-of-GB-to-low-TB hot state) cannot split MSISDN namespace across machines; vertical scaling only, which structurally rules out the very largest carriers as v0 buyers though it leaves MVNOs / IoT-MVNOs / CPaaS / international wholesale carriers (bounded by E.164 prefix space) well inside scale. (6) No cross-region replication - multi-region active-active fraud platforms (centralized correlation across roaming partners, international wholesale interconnects) cannot use beava as source of truth without an external aggregation layer. (7) In-memory only with refuse-on-network-FS - buyers must accept local NVMe + WAL replay for node loss; interconnect-billing-grade durability ($6.23B IRSF settles in real currency) needs a durable downstream sink (Kafka / Postgres CDC / S3), beava does not ship one. (8) No secondary indexes / scan APIs - 'find all A-numbers calling b_prefix X with N>5 in 1m' is not a primary-key get and would need an out-of-band scan; fraud-ops hunter queries depend on this. (9) No native PII / token-field marking and no encryption-at-rest - telcos under ePrivacy / national data-retention audit will demand explicit posture (Italian DPA fined TIM EUR 27.8M in part for excessive CDR retention; CDR retention mandated 6-24 months across EU and APAC). (10) No graph-traversal primitive - IRSF chain unrolling (caller -> forwarded-to -> forwarded-to -> premium) and call-forwarding-loop detection is a graph problem, not a primary-key get; Neo4j / TigerGraph / Memgraph fit better here. (11) No CDR-format adapters - SBC, SMSC, billing-mediation vendors emit different schemas (3GPP TS 32.298 ASN.1 BER, RADIUS-Accounting, plain CSV, JSON, Avro, proprietary push); v0 expects the user to normalise, which is a real adoption cost. (12) No native GSMA IRSF Prevention / GLF / i3Forum / IPRN hot-list ingest helper with 20-second refresh + atomic swap - every competitor either subscribes to GSMA IRSF Prevention directly or replicates the data, beava has no integration. (13) No Kafka source/sink connector - the streaming-pipeline-shop subset of buyers (~half the carrier-side market) runs Kafka in the middle and beava ships no native consumer; another sidecar-cost item. (14) No SOC 2 Type II / no published security posture - table stakes for any CPaaS-vendor buyer and a hard procurement filter for tier-1 carrier security teams. (15) No deterministic-replay-from-WAL with verifiable hashes - interconnect-billing dispute resolution requires hash-chain reproducibility; current WAL is crash-safe but not interconnect-billing-grade.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 6-12mo for a credible MVNO / IoT-MVNO / CPaaS-engineering design partner offering, 12mo+ for a tier-2 CSP / international wholesale carrier offering, beyond v0 horizon for tier-1 carrier production. The first-tier procurement-non-starter gaps (TLS+mTLS+authn+RBAC, items 1-2 above) are roughly 2 months on their own. The highest-leverage telecom-specific gaps (triggers item 3, multi-tenancy + namespace ACLs item 4, GSMA IRSF hot-list ingest item 12, Kafka source/sink connector item 13) are another 3-4 months, and triggers/actions in particular is the single most-leveraged item in the entire backlog because it directly converts beava from a 'real-time-counter store' to a 'real-time-blocking actuator' which is what the buyer actually values. CDR-format adapters (item 11) for the top-3 SBC vendors (Oracle ACME, Ribbon, AudioCodes) + 3GPP TS 32.298 CGF + RADIUS-Accounting is 2-3 months on its own and would unlock the carrier-side path without requiring Kafka. SOC 2 Type II (item 14) is a separate 6-12 month calendar item that runs in parallel and is required for any CPaaS-vendor buyer. The tier-1-scale gaps (in-process sharding item 5, cross-region replication item 6, secondary indexes item 8, encryption-at-rest + PII marking item 9, graph traversal item 10, hash-verifiable WAL item 15) are 12mo+ in aggregate and are blockers for the largest global tier-1 carriers - not required for first design partners. Note: even with all of the above, telecom procurement cycles at tier-1 carriers are structurally 12-24 months per the prompt and Subex/Mobileum/LATRO have 20-year tier-1 relationships - the engineering-time figure understates the calendar-time-to-revenue for that subset. The MVNO / IoT-MVNO / CPaaS-engineering-embed path (6-12 months engineering) bypasses most of that calendar because the buyer is procurement-light, HTTP/REST-native, and explicitly competing on time-to-fraud-control.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: Zero external proof points and zero repo evidence for telecom-CDR fraud specifically. Beava-side: no publicly named users in telecom / CPaaS / MVNO / wholesale fraud, no published case study, no conference talks (no GSMA / CFCA / Commsrisk / Capacity Media / TheFastMode / MEF Anti-Fraud / GLF presence located), no GitHub Discussion / RFC threads on telecom CDR fraud located in use case 25 deep research. Repo evidence is materially weaker than for fraud (V1): no telecom-vertical demo at python/beava/demos/ (the existing python/beava/demos/fraud/ scaffold contains an e-commerce/payment-flavoured schema.json + events.jsonl with event name 'Txn', and crates/beava-bench/configs/fraud-team.json is the same payment-flavoured benchmark, neither is telecom-flavoured), no telecom-shaped workload in crates/beava-bench/, no telecom-shaped acceptance test in python/tests/v0. A dedicated python/beava/demos/telecom_cdr/ with voice_cdr / sms_edr / signalling_event shapes plus per-A-number / per-B-prefix / per-IMSI / per-cell velocity wiring is a clear gap and is the single highest-leverage repo investment for this segment. Competitor-side validation that the segment shape is real and the market is sizeable: CFCA 2025 Global Fraud Loss Survey at $41.82B (up from $38.95B in 2023, ~$3B in two years), IRSF alone $6.23B per the 2023 number with 48% of operators reporting high-volume IRSF attacks; GSMA IRSF Prevention claiming 90%+ detection on confirmed fraud with 20-second IPRN database refresh; GSMA reporting SMS AIT up 380% over 12 months; Twilio Verify Fraud Guard publicly cited at 878M+ fraud attempts blocked through 2025, $62.7M saved for Twilio customers (with earlier $82M / 747M attempt figures published), one beta customer's deployment resulting in 27% conversion increase + 42% cost-per-user decrease + $300k savings in first month / $1.57M anticipated; Mobilesquared estimating $1.15B OTP-delivery cost loss to AIT in 2023; X publicly attributing >$60M of losses to SMS pumping in 2022; Hiya now live on all three UK MNOs (Vodafone + EE + O2/Three) extending verified caller ID to ~100% of UK mobile subscribers (Mar 2026); XConnect+GSMA IRSFCheck partnership Jan 2025; Subex MTN Group 5-year deal across 14 networks + tier-1 Middle East operator multi-year renewal + tier-1 European operator extension; Mobileum's 1,000+ customer base across 150+ countries pre-bankruptcy retained post-emergence Sep 2024 though materially impaired by the Feb 2026 criminal-fraud charges against former executives. NDSS-2021 IRSF paper validating 98% accuracy / 0.28% FPR on real European-operator CDRs with exactly the feature class beava provides natively. Beava knows clearly who the buyer is (MVNO / IoT-MVNO / fintech-telco hybrid fraud-ops engineer; CPaaS engineering team building in-house AIT/Fraud Guard) but has zero published proof points and zero repo evidence to that buyer.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Compete - this is one of the more honest 'compete' verdicts in the map because the segment shape fits beava's primitive vocabulary unusually well (per-A-number / per-B-prefix / per-IMSI / per-cell velocity counters + HLL fan-out + t-digest duration distributions + ratio features are a direct match for the NDSS-2021 feature class and the public Subex / Mobileum / Neural Technologies feature lists), the buyer's latency budget (10-50 ms SBC pre-routing, 100-500 ms CPaaS OTP-send) is well inside beava's sub-ms TCP regime, the integration surface is HTTP/REST-friendly for the MVNO / IoT-MVNO / CPaaS sub-segment, the hyperscaler bundling threat is materially lower than for any other segment in the map, and the Mobileum bankruptcy + Feb-2026 criminal-fraud charges have damaged the incumbent 'safe choice' narrative for the first time in 20 years. The credible path is NOT displacing Subex / Mobileum / LATRO / BICS at tier-1 carriers - those are 12-24 month procurement cycles against 20-year relationships and beava lacks the tier-1-scale gaps (sharding, replication, encryption-at-rest, hash-verifiable WAL, graph traversal, SOC 2 Type II) for that fight. The credible path IS the velocity-feature backend for new MVNOs / IoT-MVNOs / fintech-telco hybrids and for CPaaS engineering teams (Twilio, Sinch, Vonage, Bandwidth, Plivo, Infobip + their second-tier competitors like Telnyx, Bird, MessageBird, Prelude, Fonoster) building in-house AIT/Fraud Guards - these buyers run HTTP/REST event buses today, are procurement-light, are explicitly competing on AIT-control differentiation, and reject open-core licensing of the substrate that powers their competitive differentiator. A secondary OEM-embed path with one second-tier fraud-management vendor (Heksagon, Mobik, MGCOMM, AB Handshake, Sardine SMS-pumping, TransNexus, smaller LATRO-tier players) using beava as invisible substrate behind their product is also defensible. The 6-12 month engineering plan is concrete (TLS + authn + triggers + multi-tenancy + GSMA hot-list ingest + Kafka connector + CDR-format adapters + a real python/beava/demos/telecom_cdr scaffold + SOC 2 Type II in parallel) and the prompt's strategic framing (cannot displace incumbents but COULD be the velocity-feature backend for new MVNOs / IoT-MVNOs / fintech-telco hybrids and CPaaS) is the right read. Do NOT pitch beava as a Subex / Mobileum / LATRO replacement - that is a different sale, different buyer (Head of Fraud + Head of Wholesale Risk + 20-year RAFM-vendor relationship + GSMA IRSF Prevention data licensing), and beava cannot ship the rules library, case-management UI, SBC-vendor adapter library, or GSMA IPRN data feed that defines that procurement. Pitch beava as 'the open-source Apache-2.0 velocity-feature backend for in-house IRSF/AIT/SIM-box detection - one binary, sub-millisecond reads at the SBC/SMSC hop, ~60 telecom-shaped aggregation primitives, no Kafka required'.
